simple.meaning: עֲנַף (ʻănaph) is a Hebrew word meaning “bough, branch.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עֲנַף (H6056) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 4:9, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲנַף (H6056) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֲנַף (H6056) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֲנַף (ʻănaph) / H6056 is traced through Daniel 4:9, Daniel 4:11, Daniel 4:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6056. anaph [ עֲנַף ] noun [masculine] bough (see Biblical Hebrew ענף ); — plural suffix עַנְפ֫וֺהִי Dan 4:9 ; 4:11 (twice in verse); 4:18 .

occurrences.englishText: “Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.
The tree grew, and was strong, and its height reached to the sky, and its sight to the end of all the earth.

“This dream I, king Nebuchadnezzar, have seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able; for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
